title: Evidence-driven offer evaluation and onboarding trigger playbook
author: Nina R. Shah
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a measurable, evidence-driven process for offer evaluation and the automated triggering of role-specific onboarding pathways at Redwood Inference. It replaces ad-hoc offer decisions and fragmented onboarding handoffs with a single decision matrix, a negotiation and risk log, and concrete onboarding triggers tied to role risk, compliance needs, and ramp objectives.

Who this is for:
- Hiring managers
- Recruiters and Talent Acquisition
- HR Business Partners (HRBPs)
- People Ops specialists who build onboarding curricula
- Legal and Finance for offer approvals

Goals and principles:
- Make offer decisions transparent and auditable using a standardized scorecard.
- Reduce time-to-offer while preserving quality of decision-making (target: 48-hour typical offer SLA from verbal approval).
- Trigger onboarding pathways automatically based on objective signals (role, clearance, vendor status, critical deliverables).
- Record negotiation outcomes and commitments centrally for manager and HR ownership.

Key owners and roles:
- Recruiter: manage candidate communications, prepare initial offer package, populate scorecard.
- Hiring Manager: complete technical/cultural evaluation, set ramp objectives, confirm L4/L5+ approvals.
- HRBP: ensure compliance with compensation bands and local labor law; finalize benefits language.
- Finance: sign-off on salary above band midpoint + 15% (approval threshold).
- Legal: review for contractor/consultant engagements and NDAs.

Offer evaluation process (step-by-step):
1) Populate Offer Scorecard (required before verbal offer)
   - Responsible: Recruiter + Hiring Manager
   - Required fields: role level, base salary proposed, equity award, bonus eligibility, reason for hire, candidate score (0–5) across: technical fit, problem-solving, role-specific skills, team fit, ramp risk.
   - Attach: interview scorecards, reference-check notes, and compensation benchmarking snapshot.

2) Automated Decision Matrix applies
   - If candidate_score >= 4.0 AND proposed_comp <= band_midpoint + 10% -> auto-approve (Recruiter/HRBP finalize).
   - If candidate_score between 3.0–4.0 OR proposed_comp between band_midpoint + 10% and +25% -> HRBP + Hiring Manager sign-off required.
   - If candidate_score < 3.0 OR proposed_comp > band_midpoint + 25% OR offer contains atypical clauses -> Finance + Legal review and exec sponsor.

3) Negotiation and Risk Log (template)
   - Fields to capture: candidate_request (text), impact_on_budget (Y/N), manager_commitments (Y/N), date, negotiator name, final decision.
   - All negotiated deviations from the standard package must be recorded and stored in the candidate dossier.

4) Offer SLA targets
   - Verbal offer: within 48 hours of decision to hire.
   - Written offer (signed by HRBP/Legal): within 72 hours of verbal acceptance.
   - Exception path: roles requiring external contractor conversion, export control, or security clearance: review window up to 10 business days.

Offer Scorecard (required fields — flat table representation)
- candidate_name | role | level | technical_score (0-5) | problem_solving (0-5) | team_fit (0-5) | ramp_risk (low/med/high) | aggregate_score (0-5) | proposed_comp_pct_vs_band_mid | approvals_required

Decision and approval thresholds (examples)
- Aggregate score >= 4.0 and comp <= +10% => Recruiter + HRBP sign.
- Aggregate score 3.0–3.9 or comp +10%–+25% => Hiring Manager + HRBP required.
- Aggregate score < 3.0 or comp > +25% => Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor.

Onboarding trigger taxonomy
This section maps objective signals in the scorecard and offer to an onboarding pathway. Triggers are evaluated automatically by the People Ops intake system when the candidate signs the offer.
- Role risk triggers (immediately escalate): access to PII/PHI, admin network access, SOC2 high-impact role. => Trigger: Restricted onboarding pathway (security clearance checklist, 1:1 with Security engineer before first day).
- Compliance triggers: EEA employment, contractor vs. employee conversion, background check flags. => Trigger: Extended HR/Legal onboarding (pre-hire paperwork, local labor compliance steps).
- Ramp-critical triggers: role with measurable Q1 deliverables or cross-team dependencies. => Trigger: accelerated immersion track (prestart reading list, assigned buddy, condensed 30-day objectives).
- Remote/new-country triggers: candidate located outside primary region or requiring relocation. => Trigger: remote-localization packet and payroll/accounting enrollment steps.

Onboarding pathways (short descriptions)
- Core Standard Onboarding: baseline 90-day plan with security training, benefits enrollment, manager 30/60/90 goals and weekly 1:1 cadence.
- Restricted Onboarding: additional security orientation, expedited IAM provisioning, elevated audit logging for first 30 days.
- Accelerated Immersion: preboarding reading checklist, assigned project with narrow scope, daily standups first 2 weeks, weekly deliverable reviews.
- Compliance-Extended: staged paperwork, legal sign-offs, delayed access to production until checks complete.

Manager checklist (first 30/60/90 — condensed)
- Day 0–7: complete role-specific equipment and access; schedule 30/60/90 goal alignment; introduce to buddy; assign first-week small deliverable.
- Day 8–30: weekly check-ins; confirm completion of security and compliance training; evaluate initial pass/fail on deliverable; adjust ramp plan.
- Day 31–90: bi-weekly checkpoints; evaluate against three core KPIs defined at offer; formal 90-day calibration with HRBP.

Metrics and reporting:
- Offer conversion rate (verbal -> signed) target: >= 85%.
- Time-to-offer median: <= 4 days.
- Offer approval exceptions: logged and reviewed monthly; target fewer than 5% of hires.
- Onboarding pathway accuracy: measure after 90 days if assigned pathway matched actual risk/need; target >= 90% correct routing.

Escalation and exceptions:
- Use the Hiring Exception queue for unusual packages. Exception requests must include business justification, alternate candidates considered, and an ROI statement.
- Exceptions older than 7 days without approval auto-escalate to People Ops Director.

Templates and artifacts (examples to copy into ATS or People Ops system):
1) Negotiation log CSV header: date, negotiator, field_changed, candidate_request, decision, cost_delta_to_budget, manager_comment
2) Offer email snippet: "We are excited to extend the role of <ROLE> at Redwood Inference. Your base salary will be <AMOUNT>, equity <DETAILS>, and benefits <LINK>. Please review the attached offer and return a signed copy by <DATE>."
3) 30/60/90 Goals template: three objectives per period, success criteria, owner, and measurement method.

Related playbooks and references:
- Structured hiring committee protocol (link in related_pages).
- Manager 30/60/90 templates (People Ops templates library).

Revision history and governance:
- This playbook is maintained by People Ops (owner: Nina R. Shah).
- Review cycle: annually or after any significant comp band or legal change.
- Change approvals: HRBP + Head of People for policy changes; People Ops Director for process changes.

Appendix: example offer approval email subject
- Subject: "Approval Request: Offer for <Candidate Name> — Role <Role> — Level <L#> — Compensation uplift <+X%>"

End of document.
